statement.p: Suppose that z is a linear function of x and y with slope -1 in the x direction and slope 1 in the y direction.
(a) A change of -0.2 in x and 0.4 in y produces what change in z?
(b) If z=4 when x=2 and y=7, what is the value of z when x=1.7 and y=7.2?

static.solution:
(a) Since z is a linear function of x and y with slope -1 in the x direction, and slope 1 in the y direction, we have: z = -1 x + 1 y + c. We can write an equation for changes in z in terms of changes in x and y: \Delta z = (-1 (x + \Delta x) + 1(y + \Delta y) + c) - (-1 x + 1 y + c) = -1 \Delta x + 1 \Delta y. Since \Delta x = -0.2 and \Delta y = 0.4, we have \Delta z = -1 (-0.2) + 1(0.4) = 0.6. So a -0.2 change in x and a 0.4 change in y produces a 0.6 change in z.
(b) As we know that z=4 when x=2 and y=7, the value of z when x=1.7 and y=7.2 will be z = 4 + \Delta z = 4 - 1\Delta x + 1\Delta y. where \Delta z is the change in z when x changes from 2 to 1.7 and y changes from 7 to 7.2. We have \Delta x = 1.7 - 2 = -0.3 and \Delta y = 7.2 - 7 = 0.2. Therefore, when x=1.7 and y=7.2, we have z = 4 - 1 \cdot(-0.3) + 1\cdot(0.2) = 4.5.
